blocks.title: Introduction
Historical Background: Conformal Field Theories and Quantum Groups
blocks.content:
Primary fields, introduced under a different name by Mack and Salam in the context
of higher-dimensional conformal field theories [68], were investigated in 2D by Belavin,
Polyakov, and Zamolodchikov. They recognized that the local symmetry algebra is given
by the infinite-dimensional Virasoro algebra [5], building upon previous work by Feigin
and Fuchs [29] and Kac [62] on its representation theory.
Witten introduced an interacting 2D conformal field theory, now known as the Wess-
Zumino-Witten (WZW) model [103]. He showed that this model possesses a symmetry

Abstract. This paper establishes connections between a problem posed by Doplicher
and Roberts in the 1990s regarding construction of quantum gauge groups associated to
the category of localized endomorphisms of conformal nets, and a problem by Huang con-
cerning a direct proof of the Finkelberg equivalence theorem. We also unify the treatment
of high dimensional algebraic QFT with the low dimensional case, r

blocks.title: Quantum symmetries and primary field reconstruction in low-dimensional AQFT
blocks.content:
AQFT. In low-dimensional quantum field theories (specifically in two and three space-
time dimensions), the categories of superselection sectors naturally admit a braided tensor
structure rather than a symmetric one. Consequently, the standard DHR Bose-Fermi alter-
native does not hold any longer, allowing for the existence of non-integer statistics. Early
models exhibiting such behavior were first constructed by Streater and Wilde. The DHR
theory of superselection sectors was subsequently generalized to accommodate braid group
statistics by Fredenhagen, Rehren, and Schroer [32, 33], who showe

blocks.title: Unitary coboundary weak Hopf algebras AW(g, q)
blocks.content:
The notion of weak quasi-Hopf algebra was first introduced by Mack and Schomerus
motivated by the work of Drinfeld on quasi-Hopf algebras, specifically the Drinfeld-Kohno
theorem [70].
The weakness refers to a non-unital coproduct, and is needed to construct a coalgebra
structure on the quotient A of Uq(g) with q a root of unity by the ideal of elements
annihilated by representations with zero quantum dimension.
Since the ideal is not a
coideal, the quotient algebra A is not a bialgebra in the natural way. For sl2, Mack and
Schomerus defined a weak coproduct on A and an associator derived from

The semisimple ∗-algebra AW(g, q) := Nat(W) of natural transformations of W admits a natural structure of unitary compatible coboundary weak Hopf algebra derived from C(g, q) and W. Thanks to Theorem 29.4 in [10]–our version of Drinfeld-Kohno theorem–the Zhu algebras A(Vgk) become unitary coboundary weak quasi-Hopf algebras with a Drinfeld twist from AW(g, q), by our version of Drinfeld-Kohno theorem. This is summarized in the following section, and detailed in Sect. 33 of [10].

blocks.title: Outlook
blocks.content:
In Doplicher-Roberts theory, a unique gauge compact subgroup of SU(d) is in particular
constructed in the case of a rigid symmetric tensor C∗-category with simple unit and a
single generating object, to describe the category when the generating property of the per-
mutation group is not satisfied. Their theory has applications to the category of localized
endomorphisms arising from the local observable algebras in high dimensional AQFT, and
leads to the construction of the field algebra [20], [21].
